correctness.rationale: Reconstructed exact quantile equation p=(1+x/(2b))e^(−x), b=1+α>1, x=α/Qp(α)>0. Differentiating yields x_b=−x/[b(2b+x−1)]. The logarithmic derivative of quantile hazard is −N/[b(b−1)(2b+x−1)^2], N=4b³+4b²x−2b²+bx²−2b−2x+1. Independent SymPy algebra confirms this identity and N(1,x)=(x+1)^2, ∂_bN(1,x)=x²+8x+6, ∂²_bN=24b+8x−4>0, proving strict sign for all parameters. Equal CDF means equal survival so density shares hazard-jump sign. Numeric before/after hazards at (α1,α2,p)=(1.5,0.7,0.4) are about 0.46481 and 1.11772, corroborative only.

final_claim: For the inverted Z–Lindley law F(t;α)=(1+α/[2(1+α)t])exp(−α/t), every α>0 and p∈(0,1) satisfy d/dα h(F^−1(p;α);α)<0; the cumulative-exposure switch preserves p, so decreasing α strictly raises hazard and density at the switch; increasing α reverses the sign and equality gives continuity. This is a matched-CDF statement, not a same-age hazard comparison.
limitations: Specific to α>0, p in (0,1), IZL and CDF-matched stress switches; no whole-trajectory comparison.
